case_studies.title: Consumer tracking/audio device placed by a household member
case_studies.device_class: Retail combined location-beacon / audio-capable device (consumer 'item finder' class) — not purpose-built surveillance equipment
case_studies.rf_signature: Bluetooth Low Energy advertising bursts in the 2.4 GHz ISM band; short periodic transmissions with no fixed carrier; amplitude markedly stronger inside the premises than at the exterior reference
case_studies.discovery: Flagged by interior-vs-exterior amplitude comparison during a residential sweep, localized room-by-room, and physically recovered from a concealed position in a shared living area
case_studies.case_history: Composite of residential engagements: a minor in the household, recently disciplined, placed a consumer tracking/audio device to monitor a parent's conversations and movements. The device was an inexpensive retail product configured with a household phone.
case_studies.lessons: Most placements are by people already inside the home, using cheap consumer hardware. Insider access plus a recent grievance is the most common pattern; the response is usually a family conversation, not law enforcement.

case_studies.title: Vehicle tracking and audio kit placed by a partner of a household dependent
case_studies.device_class: Magnetic-mount GPS tracker with cellular uplink; separate battery-powered audio transmitter; companion phone-mirroring software on the subject's handset
case_studies.rf_signature: Tracker: brief cellular uplink bursts, most frequent while the vehicle is in motion. Audio transmitter: continuous narrowband carrier in the VHF/UHF range, strongest near the vehicle. Phone mirroring produces no distinctive RF signature of its own — it is found by reviewing the handset, not by spectrum sweep
case_studies.discovery: Ambient reference sweep at the curb versus readings at the vehicle showed locally-sourced signals; directional antenna work localized the tracker to the rear wheel area and the transmitter under the dash; a follow-up review of the phone found the mirroring profile
case_studies.case_history: Composite of vehicle engagements: the partner of a household dependent deployed multiple devices in the dependent's car — a GPS tracker and an audio transmitter — alongside mirroring software on their phone, as part of a pattern of coercive monitoring.
case_studies.lessons: Vehicles are high-yield: where one device is found, look for more. An RF sweep alone cannot rule out phone-level compromise — pair it with a handset review. Where monitoring is part of a coercive pattern, we discuss safety planning and appropriate referrals with the client.
